author_role: 8 desert resorts in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah compared on nightly price, drive time, private pools, breakfast and room size
lead: For most people staying in Dubai, the desert resort to book is Bab Al Shams at €443 a night: 45 minutes from the city, a 9.3 guest score, three pools and four restaurants. For your own pool, the Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi gives you a 158 m² villa with breakfast for €620; the splurge is Al Maha from €992, and the cheapest is Telal in Al Ain at €260.

The catch most visitors miss: only three of these eight are in Dubai itself; the rest are in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah, up to a 2-hour drive beyond Abu Dhabi. All eight were compared on price for the same night, drive time, guest and location score, private pool, breakfast and room size. Filter by Dubai, private pool, families, couples or budget below, or jump to the comparison table.

review: Bab Al Shams is the desert resort we would book for most people staying in Dubai. For €443 a night you get a 5★ resort designed like a walled Arab village, set inside the Al Marmoom Reserve on Al Qudra Road, about 45 minutes from the city centre. That is close enough for a one-night escape, and the guest score (9.3 from 1,768 reviews) is backed by more stays than any other resort here.

It is also the most complete resort at its price: three pools (one infinity, one shallow kids' pool), a spa with sauna and steam room, and four restaurants, including Al Hadheerah for a Middle Eastern grill dinner. Location (9.5), cleanliness (9.7) and facilities (9.6) all score high.

Against Al Maha (#3), you give up a private pool and full-board package but pay less than half. Against the Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi (#2), you get a much shorter drive from Dubai but a far smaller room: 37 m² versus a 158 m² villa.

The catches: the €443 room faces the palm courtyard (the Desert View room is €464), breakfast adds about €78 (€521 with free cancellation), and on top come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night. Bring cash for the AED 500 deposit.

review: The Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi is the best deal on this page if what you want is your own pool in the desert. The cheapest unit is not a room but the Al Rimal Pool Villa: 158 m², a private pool on a wooden deck facing the desert, and breakfast included for €620. That works out at about €3.90 per m², a third of what Bab Al Shams charges per m².

All 101 villas sit in the Al Wadi Nature Reserve in Ras Al Khaimah. The resort runs falconry, horse riding, archery, stargazing and camel treks, and its spa, The Rainforest, is a 16-station hydrothermal circuit. Dining is Kaheela (all day), Paddock Café (lunch) and a Zuma pop-up (Japanese, dinner); Farmhouse by Syrco was listed as temporarily closed.

Compared with Al Maha (#3), you pay €372 less for a villa twice the size, but you don't get Al Maha's full-board package or its location inside Dubai. Guest scores are close: 9.4 here, 9.4 at Al Maha.

The catch is distance: this is the only resort here in Ras Al Khaimah, so plan it as a two-night stay rather than an evening trip. On top of the €620 come a 10.5% service charge, a 7% destination charge, 5% VAT and an AED 20 tourism fee per night.

review: Al Maha is the most exclusive desert stay on this page. There are only 42 Bedouin-style villas, each with a temperature-controlled private pool, a sun deck and a soaking tub, set in a reserve where gazelles and other wildlife roam freely. You reach it on an 8 km sand road from the gate, about 45 minutes from Dubai.

The money buys a package rather than a room. Guests can join two activities (falconry at dawn, a dune drive or a nature walk), and full-board rates cover breakfast, a 3-course lunch and a 5-course dinner at Al Diwaan, whose deck looks over the desert. High tea is set up on the Hajar Terrace in the afternoon.

Against the Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi (#2) you pay €372 more for half the villa space, but you stay in Dubai, get the activities and can go full board. Against Bab Al Shams (#1) you get your own pool and only 42 villas, at more than double the price.

Budget for the extras: the €992 rate does not list meals, and the two-adult full-board rate is €1,673, free to cancel until 30 December and paid before arrival. A 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night are added.

review: If you picture a desert resort as a castle surrounded by tall dunes, this is it. Qasr al Sarab sits in the Liwa Desert, a 2-hour drive from Abu Dhabi, and it is the best-rated resort on this page at 9.6, with location, cleanliness and comfort all at 9.8.

For €570 with breakfast you get a 48 m² Deluxe Balcony Room facing the desert valley, a soaking bath and a pillow menu. The resort is built for a stay of several days: the Desert Excursion Centre runs camel treks, dune bashing and desert walks, there is horse riding, archery, mountain biking and tennis, an Anantara Spa with hammam, and six restaurants.

It is also the only resort here with a kids' club, which makes it the strongest family pick if you are willing to drive. Compared with Al Wathba (#5), the other Abu Dhabi option, it costs €211 more but includes breakfast and puts you deep in the Liwa dunes.

The catches: the cheapest rate is paid before arrival and is only free to cancel until 14 December 2026; pool villas start at €1,066. A 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 4% municipality fee and a 4% tourism fee are added.

review: Al Wathba is the value pick among the top-rated desert resorts. For €359 you get a 45 m² Superior room with a balcony and desert landscape views in a 5★ Luxury Collection resort, 48 km from Zayed International Airport in Abu Dhabi. The guest score is 9.3, the same as Bab Al Shams.

Compared with Qasr al Sarab (#4), it is far easier to reach (48 km from the airport against 2 hours from Abu Dhabi), but breakfast is not in the lowest rate.
Half board for two is €475, with free cancellation and pay at the property. A 10% service charge, 5% VAT and 4% each for the municipality fee, tourism fee and destination tax come on top.

review: Al Marmoom Dome is the small alternative to the big resorts. Its domes sit in the Al Marmoom Oasis, 40 km from Dubai's centre, and the €930 price (€837 with a free member sign-in) is for its cheapest private-pool unit: a 62 m² dome with a private pool, a glass ceiling over the bed, a bath and walk-in shower, a terrace with lake views and breakfast included, with free cancellation.

It is the cheapest way on this page to get your own pool inside Dubai: €62 less than Al Maha (#3), with breakfast included. The trade-off is facilities: no restaurants or spa are listed, so meals are breakfast, room service and the barbecue, unless you book the half-board, full-board-with-experiences or all-inclusive versions.

Families do well here: cots for under-4s are always free and extra beds for children 4–11 are free on request, with indoor and outdoor play areas. Horse riding is close by, and there is a tour desk for trips.
Comfort and staff both score 9.8, but value for money is 8.7. Check-in closes at 23:30, so plan the drive out of the city with that in mind.

review: Moon Retreat is the pick for a proper glamping night. Its tents and domes stand in Sharjah's desert with mountain views, off the E55 at Al Shuwaib, 64 km from Sharjah International Airport. The €400 One-Bedroom Tent is 35 m² with a king bed, air conditioning, a private bathroom, a terrace with its own barbecue and breakfast included.

The upgrade worth knowing is the Desert Pool Dome at €565: the same size, with a private pool. That makes it the cheapest private pool on this page, €55 less than the Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi (#2), though the dome is 35 m² against 158 m² there. Families can look at the 80 m² Two-Bedroom Pool Tent, €754 for two adults (add the children to see their price).

It is not a resort. There is a shared pool, an outdoor fireplace and a barbecue area, but no restaurant or spa is listed, and there are no cots or extra beds. Compared with Bab Al Shams (#1), you save €43 and get a tent with breakfast instead of a resort room without it.
The €400 rate is non-refundable; for €421 you get free cancellation until 12 January and pay at the property. A 10% service charge, 5% VAT and a 10% municipality fee are added.

review: Telal is the budget way into a desert resort. From €260 a night (€234 for members with a free sign-in) you get a 56 m² Heritage Deluxe Room with a terrace and a bathtub in a 5★ resort in the desert outside Al Ain, about an hour from Abu Dhabi International Airport. guide.h2: Desert Resorts Compared: Price, Distance, Private Pool and Breakfast
guide.html:
All eight prices are the lowest public nightly rate for two adults on the same January weeknight, before service charges and taxes. * Members who sign in for free pay less: €837 at Al Marmoom Dome and €234 at Telal. The number that changes the picture is space per euro: the Ritz-Carlton's 158 m² pool villa costs €3.90 per m², about a third of Bab Al Shams, Qasr al Sarab or Moon Retreat. Four of the eight include breakfast at the lowest price; three give you a private pool.

guide.h2: Which Desert Resort Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Best all-round, inside Dubai: #1 Bab Al Shams, €443. 45 minutes from the centre, 9.3 score, three pools, four restaurants.
  • Your own pool for the least money: #2 Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi, €620 for a 158 m² villa with breakfast. In Dubai itself: #6 Al Marmoom Dome, €930 with breakfast.
  • The splurge: #3 Al Maha, from €992 (full board €1,673 for two), with two activities and wildlife outside your villa.
  • Deepest desert and the top score: #4 Qasr al Sarab, €570 with breakfast, 9.6, in the Liwa Desert.
  • Families: Qasr al Sarab for its kids' club; Al Marmoom Dome for free extra beds up to 11; #8 Telal for the most activities on a budget.
  • Best value above 9: #5 Al Wathba, €359, 45 m² balcony room and six restaurants.
  • A tent under the stars: #7 Moon Retreat, €400 with breakfast, or €565 with a private pool.
  • Lowest price: #8 Telal, €260, in Al Ain.

Want the desert for an evening without the overnight? Compare 10 Dubai desert safaris side by side or read our one-pick desert safari verdict. Staying in the city instead? See the best luxury hotels in Dubai and Dubai hotels with a private pool.

guide.h2: Planning a Desert Stay: Location, Extra Costs and Activities
guide.html:
Dubai desert or a day's drive?

  • Inside Dubai (Bab Al Shams, Al Maha, Al Marmoom Dome): Bab Al Shams and Al Maha are about 45 minutes from the city, and Al Marmoom Dome is 40 km from the centre. These work for a single night.
  • Abu Dhabi emirate (Al Wathba, Qasr al Sarab, Telal in Al Ain): Al Wathba is 48 km from Zayed International Airport; Telal is about an hour from Abu Dhabi's airport; Qasr al Sarab is a 2-hour drive from Abu Dhabi, deep in the Liwa Desert. Plan two nights for Qasr al Sarab.
  • Northern emirates (Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi in Ras Al Khaimah, Moon Retreat in Sharjah, 64 km from Sharjah's airport).

What costs extra

  • Taxes and fees: the nightly prices above exclude them. Dubai resorts add 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night; the Abu Dhabi resorts add 5% VAT plus 4% municipality and 4% tourism fees (Al Wathba also a 4% destination tax); Moon Retreat adds 5% VAT and a 10% municipality fee; the Ritz-Carlton adds 5% VAT, AED 20 a night and a 7% destination charge. A 10% service charge (10.5% at the Ritz-Carlton) is also added on top of the nightly prices shown.
  • Breakfast: included at Ritz-Carlton, Qasr al Sarab, Al Marmoom Dome and Moon Retreat; about €78 extra at Bab Al Shams; at Al Wathba the two-adult board option is half board at €475. Al Maha's full board is €1,673 for two.
  • Extra beds: free for 4–11 at Al Marmoom Dome; AED 150–420 a night elsewhere; not available at Bab Al Shams or Moon Retreat.
  • Deposits: Bab Al Shams takes an AED 500 cash deposit on arrival.

Activities and when to go

Al Maha lets guests join two activities (falconry, dune drive or nature walk); the other resorts list activities without saying they are included in the rate. For riding in the dunes see our Dubai horse riding comparison, and for a dawn view over the desert the best hot air balloon flights, and for faster thrills dune buggy tours. The rates here are for mid-January, in the cool season.

faqs.q: What is the best desert resort in Dubai?
faqs.a: Bab Al Shams, from €443 a night: a 9.3-rated 5★ resort in the Al Marmoom Reserve, about 45 minutes from the city, with three pools and four restaurants. For a private-pool villa and full board inside Dubai, Al Maha is the luxury pick from €992.

faqs.q: How much does a desert resort near Dubai cost per night?
faqs.a: For two adults on a January weeknight, the eight compared here ran from €260 (Telal, Al Ain) to €992 (Al Maha, Dubai). Resorts scoring 9 or more start at €400 with breakfast (Moon Retreat) or €359 without (Al Wathba), and private-pool villas or domes at €620 (Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi, with breakfast). Taxes and tourism fees come on top.

faqs.q: Which desert resorts have a private pool?
faqs.a: At the lowest price: Al Maha (every villa, from €992), the Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi (every villa, €620 with breakfast) and Al Marmoom Dome (€930 with breakfast, €837 for signed-in members). Moon Retreat's Desert Pool Dome is €565 and Qasr al Sarab's pool villas start at €1,066. More options in our private-pool hotels in Dubai.

faqs.q: Is Al Maha or Bab Al Shams better?
faqs.a: Bab Al Shams for a full resort at a lower price (€443, three pools, four restaurants, kids welcome with free cots). Al Maha for privacy and an all-in package: 42 villas with private pools, two activities and full board at €1,673 for two. Both are about 45 minutes from Dubai and score 9.3 and 9.4.

faqs.q: Which desert resort is best for families?
faqs.a: Anantara Qasr al Sarab has the only kids' club (free cots up to 4). Al Marmoom Dome gives free extra beds to children 4–11 and has play areas. Telal is the budget pick with camel rides, sandboarding and a zipline, though children 6+ pay as adults.

faqs.q: How far are the desert resorts from Dubai?
faqs.a: Bab Al Shams and Al Maha are about 45 minutes from the city and Al Marmoom Dome 40 km from the centre. Al Wathba is in Abu Dhabi, 48 km from Zayed International Airport; Telal is in Al Ain; Qasr al Sarab is 2 hours from Abu Dhabi in the Liwa Desert; the Ritz-Carlton Al Wadi is in Ras Al Khaimah and Moon Retreat in Sharjah.

faqs.q: Is a desert resort better than a desert safari?
faqs.a: A safari gives you the dunes for one evening at a fraction of the price; a resort gives you the sunset, the night and the morning after, with a pool and a proper bed. If you only have one evening, compare our Dubai desert safaris.

methodology: We compared 13 desert, polo and mountain properties around Dubai on live prices for the same night (two adults, one night in mid-January) and kept the 8 that are genuinely in the desert: dunes, a desert reserve or an oasis, across Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, from €260 to €992. Each was scored on the nightly price, guest and location score, the size of the cheapest unit, private pool, breakfast cost, child policies, activities and distance from the city. Rankings reward the best all-round desert stay first, then the clearest pick for each type of traveller.
